questions.question: US imports Russian diesel by October 31?
questions.resolution_criteria:
On October 9, 2026, Donald Trump announced an agreement with Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel fuel, and the United States Treasury issued General License 135 authorizing the importation of Russian-origin diesel fuel into the United States through April 7, 2027 (see: https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117412435306815143 & https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261009_33).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Russian diesel fuel is imported to the United States between market creation and October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Russian diesel fuel refers to diesel fuel of Russian production origin.

Imported to the United States refers to the diesel fuel being physically delivered to a United States port or into the terrestrial territory of the United States for commercial or government use within the United States. Diesel fuel carried as a vessel’s own fuel, held in bond for re-export, or passing through the United States in transit to another country will not qualify.

To qualify, the import must either be described by a consensus of credible reporting as having been made under the agreement announced on October 9, 2026 (or any amended or successor arrangement between the governments of the United States and Russia), or be authorized under General License 135 (or any amended or successor authorization permitting the importation of Russian-origin diesel fuel).

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

questions.question: Will the next Google Gemini Pro model be released by October 31, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Google's next Gemini Pro model is made available to the general public between market creation and the specified date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any Gemini model released after market creation and labeled as "Pro" may qualify (e.g., gemini-3.2-pro, gemini-3.5-pro, or gemini-4.0-pro-preview). Gemini models labeled only as Flash, Flash-Lite, or another non-Pro variant will not qualify.

Products labeled as a GA promotion of an already-existing Preview model (e.g., gemini-3.1-pro-ga) may qualify

A qualifying model must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be either clearly defined and publicly announced by Google as being accessible to the general public or otherwise made publicly accessible and explicitly labeled within the company's official website. Labeling errors, placeholder text, or version names displayed on the website that do not correspond to a model that is actually accessible to the general public will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Google, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

questions.question: Will US GDP growth in Q3 2026 be greater than 3.0%?
questions.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q3 of 2026, scheduled for October 29, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

If the advance estimate is not released, this market will resolve based on the first officially published figure for real GDP for the specified quarter (e.g., the ‘second’ or ‘third’ estimate, etc.), as reported by the BEA. If no official estimate is released by the date the next quarter's advanced estimate is scheduled to be published, this market will resolve based on the most recent previous figure released by the BEA.

questions.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro win the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by less than 4%?
questions.resolution_criteria:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

questions.question: Diesel export ban before midterms?
questions.resolution_criteria:
Resolution criteria

This market will resolve to YES if the United States federal government enacts a ban or embargo on the export of diesel fuel (distillate fuel oil) from the U.S. at any point before the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to NO.

To qualify:

The action must be federal, implemented via an executive order, a federal agency action (e.g., from the Department of Energy or the Bureau of Industry and Security), or federal legislation signed into law. State-level proposals, actions, or non-binding resolutions do not qualify.

The policy must legally prohibit or comprehensively restrict the export of U.S. diesel fuel to foreign markets (temporary bans or short-term emergency embargoes qualify, but narrow, non-binding guidelines or routine administrative export licensing adjustments do not).

The ban must be officially announced and scheduled to take effect or be in effect prior to November 3, 2026.

Credible financial and political news sources—such as Bloomberg, Reuters, or The Wall Street Journal—will be used to verify the outcomes.

questions.question: Will Trump declare a national emergency before the midterms?
questions.resolution_criteria:
Shadow strategist Bannon seems to believe so. 

Resolution criteria

This market resolves to YES if Donald Trump, in his capacity as President of the United States, officially declares a new national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.) on or before November 3, 2026 (11:59 PM EST).

Source of Truth: The declaration must be officially published as a Presidential Proclamation or Executive Order on the Federal Register (federalregister.gov) or the official White House website (whitehouse.gov).

Exclusions: This market requires a newly declared national emergency. The continuation, extension, or modification of existing national emergencies (such as the January 2025 emergency regarding energy and critical minerals) will not qualify.

If no qualifying new national emergency is officially declared by the deadline, the market resolves to NO.

Background

In July and August 2026, key allies of Donald Trump—including former White House strategist Steve Bannon and media host Wayne Allyn Root—publicly urged the President to declare a national security emergency to assert federal control over the upcoming 2026 midterm elections. Proponents of this move suggest it could be used to implement voting restrictions, such as strict photo ID and citizenship requirements, or station ICE agents at polling places.

Legal scholars and critics have heavily disputed the legality of such an action, noting that the U.S. Constitution explicitly grants individual states and Congress—not the executive branch—the authority to administer federal elections. Trump himself has publicly declined to rule out the idea, stating in an August 2026 interview that "stranger things have happened" when asked about declaring an election-related emergency.

Update 2026-08-22 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): To resolve to YES, any newly declared national emergency must have the effect of disrupting the midterms.

Routine declarations (such as foreign sanctions) will not qualify unless they disrupt the midterms.

The mechanism of disruption matters less than the declaration itself.

Update 2026-08-23 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): * The market's subtext (disrupting or asserting control over the midterms) governs the resolution criteria.

Routine trade or foreign sanctions (such as Cuba- or Venezuela-style sanctions) will not qualify for a YES resolution.

Update 2026-08-24 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): - A qualifying declaration must have the practical effect of disrupting or asserting federal authority over the midterms, regardless of its stated basis (such as using foreign interference as a pretext).

Routine foreign sanctions or trade declarations do not qualify.

Final resolution is subject to creator judgment.
